To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the minority carrier lifetimes measured in n- and p- type AlGaAs/Gas quantum wells grown by molecular beam epitaxy are strongly dependent on growth temperature and on the form of the arsenic source used.

(1) minority carrier lifetimes are nearly an order magnitude lower than radiative lifetimes in lightly doped Al0.25Ga0.75As/GaAs structures grown by solid-source molecular beam epitaxy at 600-700 degrees C, and (2) they are nearly an order lower than radiative values in both n- and p- type samples, which is consistent with recombination via an acceptor-type centre.

the minority carrier lifetimes in AlGaAs-GaAs quantum well heterostructures grown by solid source MBE depend strongly on growth temperature when the arsenic is supplied as As4, but are essentially independent of growth temperature if the arsenic is provided as As2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the properties of semiconductor materials, in particular the growth and characterisation of III-V semiconductor structures.
the growth of GaAs/AlGaAs quantum well structures for use in optoelectronic devices.
the growth, characterisation and modelling of AlGaAs/Gas quantum well structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the lifetime measurements are not in conflict with the radiative lifetimemeasurements, but they do suggest that the lifetime measurements do not reflect a recombination process which is independent of growth temperature.
the recombination lifetime in these structures is determined by the density of a deep acceptor in the Al-containing regions.
the lifetime measurements are consistent with a model involving recombination via a deep acceptor in the Al-containing layers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lifetime in the quantum well is dominated by the recombination lifetime in the barrier material.

the growth of high-quality AlGaAs/GaN structures is not sensitive to growth temperature in the range 600 to 700 degrees C, but the growth of GaAs/GaN structures with high minority carrier lifetimes is.
, for these particular structures, a growth temperature of 675 degreesC, using As2, gives the best combination of low defect density and long lifetime.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the growth of high quality, low lifetime AlGaAs/Gas quantum well material is readily achievable, and is not particularly sensitive to growth temperature.

the use of As2 as the source of group V atoms during molecular beam epitaxy growth of AlGaAs/Gas quantum wells can lead to significantly longer minority carrier lifetimes than are obtained when As4 is the source.
it should be possible to grow high quality, long lifetime quantum well structures by solid source MBE, provided that care is taken to avoid oxygen incorporation.
